read_kelvin.description: Read the temperature of a sensor input in kelvin; RDGST? is read after it, and a reading with an invalid, underrange or overrange status is kept as uncertain.

read_status.description: Read the status of a sensor input as the sum of its flags: 0 a valid reading; 1 invalid reading, 16 temperature underrange, 32 temperature overrange, 64 sensor units zero, 128 sensor units overrange.

read_setpoint.description: Read the setpoint of a control loop, in the preferred units of its control sensor.

set_setpoint.description: Set the setpoint of a control loop, in the preferred units of its control sensor (kelvin when the sensor's units are kelvin).

read_heater.description: Read the output of heater 1 or 2 in percent of full scale. Outputs 3 and 4 are read with AOUT?.

read_range.description: Read the range of heater 1 or 2: 0 off, 1 low, 2 medium, 3 high.

set_range.description: Set the range of heater 1 or 2: 0 off, 1 low, 2 medium, 3 high.

heater_error.description: Read and clear the error of heater 1 or 2: 0 no error, 1 heater open load, 2 heater short. Querying clears the error and the front panel message.

conditions.description: Heater 1 reported no open load or short since the previous observation
conditions.note: An open load is a disconnected or broken heater; a short is a heater or lead shorted. Querying clears the error, so the next observation shows whether it returned. A temperature controlled through this output while it delivered no power was not held at its setpoint.

conditions.description: Heater 2 reported no open load or short since the previous observation
conditions.note: As for heater 1. Experiments that use only heater 1 require heater1_ok; selected-condition maintenance can omit this output.
